recipes.title: Rasam
recipes.description: Thin, peppery South Indian tamarind and tomato soup, served over rice.

steps.instructionText: For the rasam powder, toast the coriander seeds, 4 of the chillies, the cumin and the asafoetida in the oil until lightly browned.
Grind the toasted spices to a powder.
Wash the toor dal until the water runs clear.
Cook the dal with double its volume of water and the turmeric for 30 minutes, until mushy.
Quarter the tomatoes and bring them to the boil in a saucepan of water.
Add the tamarind, salt and sugar, a little tamarind at a time.
When the tomatoes are half cooked, add the cooked dal and 4-5 tsp of the rasam powder. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Heat the ghee in a small pan. Fry the mustard seeds, urad dal, remaining chillies and curry leaves until the dal browns.
Pour the seasoning into the rasam and stir it through.
Add the coriander leaves and serve with hot boiled rice.

recipes.title: Aloo Tikki (Twice-Fried)
recipes.description: Potato halves deep-fried until tender, pressed flat, fried again till golden and dusted with spices.

steps.instructionText: Peel and halve the potatoes, then sprinkle them with salt.
Heat the oil for deep frying. Fry the potatoes over low heat until tender, then lift them out and let them cool.
Place the potatoes on a board and gently flatten each one with the palm of your hand.
Deep fry the flattened potatoes again until golden.
Sprinkle each with a little red chilli powder, amchur and coriander powder, and serve hot.

recipes.title: Banana Curry
recipes.description: Firm bananas simmered gently in a creamy, lightly spiced milk sauce with cumin and turmeric.

steps.instructionText: Peel the bananas and cut them into 2 cm slices.
Add the milk, fresh cream, garam masala, chilli powder, lemon juice and a little salt to the bananas.
Melt the butter, add the cumin seeds and turmeric powder, and cook for 2 minutes over medium-low heat, until fragrant.
Add the bananas and their sauce.
Cook on a gentle flame until the bananas are just tender. Do not overcook.

recipes.title: Basic Indian Tomato Gravy
recipes.description: Simple onion-tomato curry base with ginger, garlic and ground spices, ready for vegetables, eggs or chicken.

steps.instructionText: Heat the ghee and fry the onion until it starts to brown.
Add the ginger paste and garlic and stir, then add the chilli powder, coriander powder, cumin powder and turmeric powder. Mix well.
Add the tomatoes and salt to taste.
Turn the heat to medium, cover and cook for 10 minutes, until it forms a thick, spicy gravy.
Use the gravy as a base for vegetables, boiled eggs, paneer or chicken, and serve with plain rice.

recipes.title: Pani Puri
recipes.description: Crisp puris filled with potato, moong and tamarind chutney, then topped up with chilled spiced water.

steps.instructionText: For the pani, blend the chaat masala, amchur, jeera powder, coriander powder, red chilli powder, black pepper, hing, lemon juice and black salt with chilled water. Chill it.
Boil the potatoes and the moong dal separately until soft.
Peel the potatoes and roughly mash them.
Soak the tamarind in a little hot water, squeeze out the pulp and simmer it with the sugar into a thick chutney. Chill it.
Break a small hole in the top of each puri.
Fill each puri with potato, moong dal, a few boondi, coriander leaves and a little tamarind chutney.
Pour in the chilled pani and eat at once.

recipes.title: Chicken Tikka
recipes.description: Boneless chicken cubes marinated in spiced yogurt, then skewered and grilled until cooked through.

steps.instructionText: Cut the chicken breast into bite-sized cubes.
In a non-metal bowl, mix the mustard oil, milk, yogurt, lemon juice, tomato paste, coriander leaves, garlic, red chillies, paprika, garam masala, cumin powder, turmeric and salt.
Add the chicken and mix until fully coated.
Cover and marinate in the fridge overnight, ideally for 24 hours.
Thread the chicken onto skewers.
Grill the chicken under a medium grill for 8 minutes.
Turn the skewers and grill the other side of the chicken for 8 minutes, until cooked through.
Check that the chicken comes apart easily when pressed with a fork, then serve with naan or rice.

recipes.title: Chana Dal Masala
recipes.description: Soaked chana dal cooked soft and tossed in a fried onion-tomato masala with chillies, ginger and pepper.

steps.instructionText: Soak the chana dal in water overnight.
Drain the chana dal and pressure cook it until tender. Drain well.
Fry the onions in hot oil until golden brown.
Add the tomatoes and fry until the oil separates.
Add the green chillies, ginger and salt.
Add the red chilli powder and the drained chana dal. Boil for 2 minutes.
Stir in the black pepper and garam masala, and garnish with the coriander leaves.
Serve hot with roti or naan.

recipes.title: Churri (Yogurt Herb Sauce)
recipes.description: Cool blend of yogurt and buttermilk with ground mint, coriander, ginger, green chilli and toasted cumin.

steps.instructionText: Toast the cumin seeds in a dry pan over medium heat until fragrant, without letting them burn.
Grind the toasted cumin seeds in a mortar.
Chop the mint leaves, coriander leaves, ginger and green chillies, then grind them to a paste.
Add the yogurt, buttermilk and salt and mix everything together well.
Chop the onion and stir it in with the ground cumin seeds.

recipes.title: Coconut Chutney (North Indian)
recipes.description: Fresh coconut ground with green chilli, garlic and coriander leaves into a quick, punchy chutney.

steps.instructionText: Put the coconut, green chillies, garlic, coriander leaves, salt and water in a blender.
Grind everything well into a smooth chutney.
Serve fresh; keep leftovers in the fridge and use within 2 days.

recipes.title: Coriander Chutney
recipes.description: Fresh green chutney of coriander leaves, onion, green chilli, cumin and lemon, blended to a fine paste.

steps.instructionText: Wash the coriander leaves well.
Finely chop the onion, green chillies and coriander leaves.
Add the salt, cumin seeds and the juice of the lemon.
Blend everything to a fine paste.

recipes.title: Mirchi ka Salan
recipes.description: Hyderabadi curry of fried green chillies in a nutty sesame, poppy seed and coconut gravy soured with tamarind.

steps.instructionText: Lightly dry-roast the khus khus, til, coriander seeds, cumin seeds and desiccated coconut, then grind them in a mortar and pestle.
Heat the oil in a frying pan and stir-fry the green chillies with a little salt. Lift them out, drain and keep aside.
Heat a little of the oil in a pan. Add the dried red chillies, methi seeds and a few curry leaves and fry until they pop.
Add the onions and fry until golden brown.
Mix in the ground spices, red chilli powder, haldi, ginger garlic paste and kalonji. Stir well and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the tamarind juice and cook for 1 minute.
Add the fried green chillies and the remaining curry leaves, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Serve with biryani or plain rice.

recipes.title: Dal Makhani
recipes.description: Punjabi black urad dal and rajma, slow-simmered in a tomato masala and finished with cream and ghee.

steps.instructionText: Wash the urad dal and rajma and soak them overnight in lukewarm water.
Drain, then cook the dal and rajma in the water with salt, red chilli powder, turmeric powder and grated ginger until soft. Keep aside.
Heat the oil in a heavy pan. Add the hing, bay leaves, cinnamon stick, laung and onion, and fry until golden brown.
Add the ginger garlic paste and sauté briefly.
Add the tomatoes and coriander powder, and sauté until the tomatoes are well mashed.
Add the cooked dal and a little water as needed. Mix well and simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in the fresh cream and ghee and simmer for 5 minutes more.
Garnish with the coriander leaves and serve hot with naan, paratha or rice.

recipes.title: Cheeyam (Sweet Chana Dal Balls)
recipes.description: Tamil sweet of chana dal and jaggery dough balls, dipped in a thin maida batter and deep-fried golden.

steps.instructionText: Soak the kadalai paruppu in plenty of water for at least 8 hours; it doubles in size.
Pressure cook the kadalai paruppu with water for 9 minutes, then let the pressure drop on its own.
Drain well, then grind with the vellam and cardamom pods, without adding water, into a thick dough.
Roll the dough into small balls.
Whisk the maida with water and salt into a thin batter.
Heat the oil in a deep pan until a small piece of dough floats and bubbles when dropped in.
Dip each ball in the batter and deep fry a few at a time until golden.

recipes.title: Gobi Bhaji (Cauliflower Stew)
recipes.description: Cauliflower pressure-cooked in a spicy onion-tomato masala with green chillies, ginger and garam masala.

steps.instructionText: Boil the cauliflower in water for 5 minutes. Drain and cut it into big pieces.
Heat some oil in a pressure cooker and add the onions.
Add the tomatoes and fry until the oil separates.
Add the cauliflower, green chillies and ginger.
Add the red chilli powder and a little water. Pressure cook for 7 minutes.
Stir in the garam masala, black pepper and salt, and garnish with the coriander leaves.
Serve with chapati, naan or pulao.

recipes.title: Aam Panna
recipes.description: Tangy summer drink concentrate of cooked green mango, roasted cumin, mint and rock salt.

steps.instructionText: Cut each green mango into 3 pieces: one from each side of the seed and one with the seed.
Pressure cook the mangoes with a small cup of water, turning off the heat at the first whistle.
Let the cooker rest for 7 minutes, then open it and let the mangoes cool.
Grind the sugar, roasted cumin seeds and roasted chilli in a food processor.
Mince the mint leaves in the food processor.
Squeeze the pulp of the cooled mangoes into a blender, discarding the skins and seeds.
Purée the mango pulp until smooth.
Add the ground sugar mixture, rock salt and mint leaves, and blend well.
Pour into a clean bottle and refrigerate; it keeps for about 2 weeks.
To serve, stir 4-5 tsp of the concentrate into a glass of water.

recipes.title: Baati (Rajasthani Hard Bread)
recipes.description: Dense, unleavened wheat discs kneaded very firm, cooked in a dry pan, charred lightly and served with ghee.

steps.instructionText: Mix the wheat flour and salt.
Working with about 1 cup of the flour mixture at a time, rub in a little of the oil, breaking up any lumps.
Add water 1 tbsp at a time and knead very hard until the dough holds in a firm, compact ball. Repeat with the rest.
Let the dough balls rest for 5 minutes.
Flatten each ball by hand, then roll into smooth discs about 10 cm across and 1 cm thick.
Cook in a dry pan on a low flame. Flip once the bottom starts to harden, then pinch the top all over with two fingers.
When the bottom browns in spots, turn the baati upside-down onto a wire grate over the flame to blacken the bumps a little.
Drizzle with the ghee and serve with dal or a vegetable dish.

recipes.title: Jeera Rice with Cashews
recipes.description: Basmati rice cooked with cumin seeds, raisins and cashews for an easy, fragrant side dish.

steps.instructionText: Heat the olive oil in a pot.
Add the cumin seeds, then the raisins and cashews. Sauté for 2 minutes.
Add the basmati rice and sauté for 1 more minute.
Add the water and bring everything to the boil.
Lower the heat, cover and cook for 12 minutes.

recipes.title: Lemon Pickle (Nimbu Achar)
recipes.description: Oil-free lemon pickle with roasted mustard, methi and chilli, matured in the sun for a month or more.

steps.instructionText: Wash the small lemons and dry them completely, leaving no water on them. Trim off the stalks.
Cut the lemons into 2 cm pieces and put them in a dry bowl.
Dry-roast the methi seeds, black mustard seeds and hing in a pan for about 5 minutes over medium heat, without burning them.
Grind the roasted spices to a powder.
Add the ground spices, turmeric powder, salt, sugar, red chilli powder and lemon juice to the lemons. Mix well.
Pack into a clean, dry 2 litre jar, leaving at least 1 cm space at the top.
Put the jar in the sun each morning and bring it in each evening, for at least a month (two in winter), until it matures.

recipes.title: Chunky Mango Chutney
recipes.description: Sweet-sour chutney of under-ripe mango, raisins and onion cooked down in cider vinegar with ginger and garlic.

steps.instructionText: Peel the mangoes and cut them into cubes.
Dissolve the brown sugar and salt in the cider vinegar and boil for 15 minutes.
Add the mangoes, raisins and onion and bring back to the boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer the mangoes for 15 minutes, stirring constantly so they do not stick.
Add the garlic, ginger, cayenne and black pepper and simmer for 5 minutes.
Take off the heat and let it cool before serving.
Store in the fridge for up to 6 months.

recipes.title: Aam ki Chutney (Mango Coconut)
recipes.description: Fresh, uncooked chutney of ripe mango cubes with coconut, ginger, coriander, chilli and orange juice.

steps.instructionText: Slice the flesh off both sides of each mango stone, as close to the stone as possible, keeping the skin on.
Score each mango half in a criss-cross pattern down to the skin, making 1 cm squares.
Push the skin up from underneath to turn each half inside out, then cut the mango cubes off the skin into a small bowl.
Add the coconut, coriander leaves, ginger, cayenne pepper, orange juice and salt, and mix gently.
Chill in the fridge for 1-2 hours before serving.

recipes.title: Onion Chutney
recipes.description: South Indian red onion chutney with roasted chana dal, coconut, dried chillies and tamarind, for dosa or idli.

steps.instructionText: Heat the oil in a shallow pan. Add the chana dal and stir until it is roasted.
Add the red onions and stir-fry until transparent and golden brown at the edges.
Turn off the heat and let the mixture cool for a few minutes.
Blend the onion mixture with the coconut, dried red chillies, tamarind paste and salt to a smooth paste, adding a few teaspoons of water if needed.

recipes.title: Phulourie (Split Pea Fritters)
recipes.description: Indo-Caribbean fritters of ground split peas, garlic, cumin and turmeric, fried into small golden balls.

steps.instructionText: Soak the split peas overnight in lightly salted cold water.
Drain the split peas and grind them finely in a mixer.
Mix in the maida, baking powder, garlic, egg, salt, turmeric and ground cumin, adding enough water to make a thick dropping batter.
Heat the oil for deep frying.
Squeeze small dollops of batter between thumb and forefinger into the hot oil, making balls about 2 cm across.
Fry until golden brown, then drain on kitchen paper.
Serve hot with dal or a sour chutney.
